1. Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon — adjust downward by 1–3% for the first 5–7 days.

2. After sharp price spikes, model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% in the 3–5 day window following a spike.

3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if recent 7-day average is below 70, forecast should be capped at 70–72; if above 75, cap at 75–77.

4. Forecast lags true price movements by 2–4 days — shift forecast 2–4 days forward to align with actual price trajectory.

5. Model underestimates volatility in low-price regimes — increase forecast by 1–2% when price is below 65.

6. Model overestimates high-price regimes — reduce forecast by 3–5% when price is above 75.

7. Model fails to capture downward momentum after 3 consecutive days of rising prices — if 3-day rise, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3 days.

8. Model overfits to recent high prices — if last 5 days are above 72, reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 5 days.

9. Model underestimates downward corrections after spikes — if price spiked >5% from 30-day average, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7 days.

10. Model shows persistent bias toward 72–74 — if forecast is consistently above 74, reduce by 2–4% for next 3 days.
